title: The Snake and Jupiter
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Snake suffered a good deal from being constantly trodden upon by man and beast, owing partly to the length of his body and partly to his being unable to raise himself above the surface of the ground: so he went and complained to Jupiter about the risks to which he was exposed. But Jupiter had little sympathy for him. "I dare say," said he, "that if you had bitten the first that trod on you, the others would have taken more trouble to look where they put their feet."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Snake suffer from?
options: Being constantly trodden upon by man and beast
Being hunted by birds of prey
Losing his skin too often
Being unable to find enough food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is one reason given for why the Snake kept getting trodden upon?
options: The length of his body
His bright coloring
His habit of sleeping in open paths
His slow speed compared to other animals

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Snake unable to do?
options: Raise himself above the surface of the ground
Move quickly across open ground
Find shelter from the sun
Warn others of his presence

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who did the Snake complain to about being trodden upon?
options: Jupiter
The other snakes
The nearest farmer
A passing bird

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much sympathy did Jupiter have for the Snake's complaint?
options: A great deal
Little sympathy
Enough to punish those who trod on him
None at all, and he refused to answer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Jupiter say the Snake should have done to the first creature that trod on him?
options: Warned it loudly
Bitten it
Moved out of its way
Followed it home

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Jupiter imply the Snake should rely on to solve his own problem?
options: Divine intervention rather than his own action
The pity of the creatures who trod on him
His own means of defending himself, rather than complaining
A change in the shape of his body

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: The gods will always defend the weak against the strong
Those who suffer harm without resisting can expect the harm to continue
It is wrong to complain to Jupiter about anything
Length of body always causes misfortune

questions.prompt: According to the passage, besides man, what else is said to have trodden upon the Snake?
options: Beast
Birds
Fish
Insects

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Snake complain to Jupiter about?
options: The risks to which he was exposed
The cold weather in his burrow
The lack of food near his den
Other snakes stealing his territory

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Jupiter say would have happened if the Snake had bitten the first creature that trod on him?
options: The others would have taken more trouble to look where they put their feet
The other creatures would have stopped walking through the area entirely
Jupiter would have punished the Snake for it
The Snake would have lost his fangs afterward

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Jupiter respond to the Snake with little sympathy rather than offering help?
options: He believes the Snake's own inaction, not bad luck, is the real cause of his troubles
He is too busy with more important matters to listen
He dislikes snakes more than other creatures
He thinks the Snake is lying about being trodden upon

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "trodden upon" mean in "constantly trodden upon by man and beast"?
options: Stepped on
Chased away
Spoken about unkindly
Admired from a distance

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Snake bites Jupiter out of frustration
Jupiter punishes the creatures who trod on the Snake
The Snake complains of being trodden upon, and Jupiter tells him he should have defended himself from the start
Jupiter changes the shape of the Snake's body to protect him
